about: Forge Cellars is a partnership between two growers from very different traditions: Rick Rainey, a New York winegrower who runs the vineyards and the business, and Louis Barruol, whose family owns Château de Saint Cosme in Gigondas in the southern Rhône. Their first vintage was 2011, made on the east side of Seneca Lake, the deepest of the Finger Lakes. Justin Boyette joined as a partner and winemaker, and today the team works with around sixteen vineyards, nearly all of them on Seneca’s shores.

The “Classique” wines are Forge’s portrait of east Seneca Lake as a whole, blended from several sites rather than one, with single-vineyard bottlings made alongside them. Fruit comes from growers committed to sustainable farming, is picked by hand and fermented spontaneously with native yeasts, with as little intervention as the vintage allows. The Pinot Noir is lightly oaked, keeping the focus on fruit and the cool lake climate rather than on barrel.

Expect a cool-climate Pinot Noir in a restrained, Old World register: red and dark cherry fruit, florals and a savory, earthy edge, with fresh acidity carrying it. Critics who follow Forge regularly describe its Pinots as elegant and silky rather than heavy, which makes this an easy partner for roast chicken, pork or mushrooms off the wood fire.
